title: Gecko feet stick to the ceiling. So how can they walk? | So That's Why
description:
Little Q spots a gecko hanging upside down on the living room ceiling, not moving at all. If its feet stick to the ceiling, how does it lift them when it wants to walk?

In this episode, the Chief and Little Q follow one gecko foot all the way around: first they check whether its feet have glue or suction cups; then they draw the toes big, to see how rows of skin, hairs far finer than yours and even tinier flat pads stick with a tiny pull that works by getting close enough, in enough places; next, how a curl of the toes tips the hairs past an angle so they let go on their own, and how dirty feet come clean in a few steps; and finally non-stick pans, wet glass and bumpy walls, to see where the trick stops working.

The illustrations in this episode were made with AI; they are diagrams, not microscope photos or measurements. Most numbers in the video come from studies of the Tokay gecko and are approximate; another kind of gecko may differ. If you see a gecko, please don't try to catch it. The source of every claim is listed in the references below.
